chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The hearts of men are wild beasts; whoever tames them, they turn towards him.

key_terms.تَأَلَّفَهَا: He tamed/affectioned them (from alif-waw-lam, to win over)
key_terms.قُلُوبُ: Hearts (plural of heart, referring to inner nature/disposition)

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor for human hearts in Nahj al-Balagha and how to win people over?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of wild beasts to illustrate the untamed nature of human hearts, emphasizing that gentle persuasion and affinity (talaqqf) are essential to tame them. This teaching highlights the psychological insight that receptivity is cultivated through approachability rather than force, a principle deeply rooted in Shia ethical traditions. The hadith underscores the importance of social intelligence in leadership and personal relationships, aligning with the Quranic emphasis on wisdom and good preaching.
